items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: I was listening to Miles and you know, all that, Bud Powell.

ctx.x: Oh man. Well I’ll tell you the truth, I wasn’t into a lot of pop music at all. My brother, my older brother Torrie, Torrie Zito, he was into jazz. He was a piano player. And I used to listen to his records. He would buy records and I would just zero in. But there were some pop records that I really liked. You know like — oh I mean well actually it was rhythm and blues bands. That’s what it was you know. It was really rhythm and blues.

You know like Wilson Pickett and those people in the beginning, I just loved the rhythm feel you know in those records. But yeah “Rock Around the Clock” and those, they were okay but it was more like it just struck me as being like country you know, more country than anything else. But I know the people just loved it. But that’s about it. I listened to a lot of jazz records when I was like 14 and 15, I was listening to Miles and you know, all that, Bud Powell.
But you were playing gigs around Central New York and the Utica area probably early on.
